assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological nitrogen fixation and an exceptional problem in biological energy conversion: a complex metal cluster (FeMo-cofactor) that couples ATP hydrolysis, electron transfer and proton delivery to reduce N2. Crystal structures revealed the cofactor and its interstitial carbide, and kinetics/spectroscopy have framed a physically explicit mechanism. Importance is high in chemistry, agriculture and bioenergetics.
assessment.attribution: The structural breakthroughs (MoFe protein, Fe protein, cofactor composition and the central light atom) are attributable mainly to Rees and Einsle, while Seefeldt and colleagues supplied much of the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Dean and Ribbe made genetic and biosynthetic contributions, and the credited list omits some prominent mechanistic contributors; allocation among structure, genetics and mechanism needs expert-report support.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed independently over about three decades and the carbide assignment is well established; the catalytic cycle is only partly resolved, though recognition of the structural and mechanistic foundation is not premature.
uncertainties: The detailed N2-reduction mechanism (E4 state, substrate-binding site) is not fully settled.
Credit is split across structure, genetics and kinetics; the best three-person configuration is unclear.
I have not independently verified the relative priority of individual structural claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron tunneling through proteins is a foundational physical mechanism for biological redox chemistry, with distance and driving-force dependence and hopping pathways quantified in engineered, photo-triggered metalloproteins. It underpins how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes work and is stated in clear physical terms, which I value.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is compact and a fair prize configuration. The wider field includes theoretical contributions (Marcus-theory framework, tunneling-pathway models) that would need acknowledgement, and a prize might raise priority questions relative to other experimentalists, though the supplied credit is clean.
assessment.maturity: The work is mature, with decades of independent confirmation and broad use, so timing is not premature. A possible concern is that central ideas were partly recognized earlier through electron-transfer theory.
uncertainties: Overlap with already-recognized electron-transfer theory may limit how novel the committee views the experimental contribution.
The roles of tunneling versus multistep hopping in specific natural enzymes remain debated.
Only two names are credited; I cannot verify whether decisive contributions from others are missing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry made intact noncovalent protein complexes, membrane proteins and their stoichiometry, lipid binding and assembly pathways measurable in the gas phase, complementing structural biology. It is a method that makes biochemical mechanism visible and has wide impact on structural and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait are credible leaders in demonstrating and extending intact-complex MS, while Loo and Gross are pioneers of related ionization and methodology. The early conceptual origin versus later broad application is a real priority question; three names is workable but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently reproduced across many labs, with instruments now commercial. Recognition would be mature, although mass spectrometry has been awarded before (ESI/MALDI 2002), which affects its comparative standing.
uncertainties: Priority among the early native-MS demonstrators versus later extenders is disputed in my assessment.
Comparison with the previous MS Nobel Prize may affect appetite for recognition.
Whether the membrane-protein extension is a separate discovery is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables room-temperature, damage-outrunning structures of microcrystals and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, connecting kinetics with structure. This closely matches my interest in dynamic visualization of biochemical mechanisms, with major methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffraction-before-destruction concept and early experiments, Fromme and Hajdu were early proof-of-principle partners, and Schlichting drove time-resolved applications. Hajdu's contribution and role in the origin are credited yet the three-laureate limit forces choices; I propose Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting, with the allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Core methodology is established and reproduced at several facilities, but the scientific harvest of mechanistic results is still maturing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a physics/instrumentation advance versus chemistry.
Allocation between early concept, instrument development and biological application is unresolved.
Few fully resolved mechanisms so far relative to the promise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another at targeted genomic sites without double-strand cleavage, a clear chemical invention with large therapeutic and research impact. Clinical translation is under way, supporting lasting significance.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the principal inventor; Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments for cytosine and adenine base editors as trainees. Kondo and Nishida independently reported a related deaminase-based editor. The prime-editing candidate overlaps in the Liu lab line and a Liu-alone prize would be a possibility the allocation question must consider.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and entering the clinic, but long-term safety and efficacy data are limited, and genome editing was recognized in 2020, which may weigh on timing.
uncertainties: Overlap and ordering with CRISPR (2020) and with the separate prime-editing candidate.
Independent invention by Kondo and Nishida complicates priority.
Clinical outcomes are still immature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer describes concerted proton and electron movement central to enzymes such as cytochrome c oxidase, photosystem II and to molecular electrocatalysis, and is a field I know well. The concept and theory are fundamental, though it is a conceptual framework spanning many systems.
assessment.attribution: The candidacy is a line of work rather than one clearly attributable discovery: Meyer introduced early PCET studies, Mayer the bond-dissociation free-energy framework, Hammes-Schiffer the theory and Nocera the energy-conversion applications. Any three-person split would undercredit others.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well established and independently supported by experiment and theory, but different parts mature differently, and application to catalysis is still developing.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across theory and experiment, including omitted contributors such as Meyer.
Whether the committee sees a single discovery rather than a research program.
Possible bias from my own field, which I should disclose.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and relaxation-based solution NMR methods enabled structure and dynamics determination of large proteins and complexes, including methyl-TROSY approaches for high-molecular-weight systems and invisible conformational states. They make dynamic mechanisms experimentally accessible at atomic resolution.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are prominent for multidimensional heteronuclear methods, TROSY-related and dynamics applications, but Wagner and Palmer made foundational contributions and the work is cumulative. NMR was recognized in 1991 and 2002, so a new award must show a distinct step.
assessment.maturity: Methods are mature and ubiquitous; recognition would not be premature, though the field has previously received awards.
uncertainties: Several equally strong contributors and a cumulative rather than singular discovery.
Prior NMR Nobel Prizes may reduce appetite.
Selection of three out of five is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates formed by phase separation changed how cellular organization is understood and introduced physical-chemical principles into cell biology. The idea has had large conceptual influence across biochemistry and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like P granules and the framework, while Rosen's multivalent-interaction work is a key complementary step; Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar theory. Credit is plausibly more than three persons.
assessment.maturity: The field is young, with active debate about physiological relevance and what counts as phase separation versus other assemblies, so I consider it less mature than the other candidates on my ballot.
uncertainties: Debate on in vivo mechanisms and the quality of quantitative physical evidence.
Likely premature relative to other candidates.
Attribution beyond three people is plausible.
